title: County of Rouergue
capsule: The County of Rouergue (Roergue) was a feudal county in the southern Massif Central centred on Rodez, corresponding roughly to the modern Aveyron department. In this period it was held by the comital house of Toulouse: Raymond III of Rouergue and his successors governed it as part of the wider Toulousain patrimony, while much of the countryside lay under the rising power of local lords and the great abbeys such as Conques. Comital authority here was loose and contested, exercised amid the castle-building and seigneurial fragmentation characteristic of eleventh-century Languedoc.
